 Mike Snider USA TODAY Nov. 20, 2026, 2:17 p.m. ET Hear this story The Food and Drug Administration has expanded a recall of certain food products sold at workplaces and in vending machines for possible listeria contamination.
 Grand Strand Sandwich Company Inc., of Longs, South Carolina, is recalling several of its Lunch Box sandwiches, distributed between March 2 and Nov. 10, in clear plastic packaging and sold primarily in retail convenience stores, vending machines and prison canteens, located in North Carolina, South Carolina and Virginia, the company said in an alert on the FDA website .
 Grand Strand said it was notified on Nov. 11 that biscuits supplied by Dot Foods may be contaminated with the disease-causing bacteria Listeria monocytogenes . Dot Foods , of Mt. Sterling, Illinois, has a distribution relationship with grain-based and frozen food producer C.H. Guenther of San Antonio, Texas; biscuits made by C.H. Guenther & Son have been part of a Nov. 14 recall issued by the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS).
 Recalls: Over 51K toothpaste, mouthwash products recalled. See the list Which products were recalled?
 Grand Strand Sandwich Company said the following products – sold primarily in retail convenience stores, vending machines and prison canteens, located in North Carolina, South Carolina and Virginia – were voluntarily recalled. No illnesses have been reported to date.
 Holiday shopping: Find the best deals and gifts across tech, home, outdoors and more Lunch Box Bacon Egg and Cheese Biscuit, 4-ounce: UPC 0 67068 21400 8
 Lunch Box Chicken Sausage Biscuit, 3.75-ounce: UPC 0 67068 21404 6
 Lunch Box Jumbo Sausage Biscuit, 4-ounce: UPC 0 67068 21407 7
 Lunch Box Sausage Egg & Cheese Biscuit, 5-ounce: UPC 0 67068 21402 2
 Consumers who purchased these products are urged to return them to the place of purchase for a full refund, or discard the product. Consumers with questions may contact Grand Strand Sandwich at 843-399-2999 Monday-Thursday from 8 a.m. - 4 p.m. ET, and Friday 8 a.m. to Noon ET.
 Related products recalled: 
 Several other ready-to-eat products with biscuits made by C.H. Guenther & Son were recently recalled for potential listeria contamination, according to the FDA and USDA.
 Mmm! Meals Made in Minutes Biscuit & Sausage Gravy ready-to-eat biscuit sandwiches sold in vending machines in six states, including Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Oklahoma, Tennessee and Texas (bestby dates of Nov. 12-18).
 Fresh to You Sausage, Egg & Cheese Biscuit Sandwich distributed in break rooms, refrigerated vending machines and cafeterias, as part of the larger biscuit recall. These were sold in Alabama, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Oklahoma, Tennessee and Texas (best-by dates of Nov. 7-19).
 Fresh to You Sausage, Egg & Cheese Biscuit Sandwiches sold in Oregon and Washington between Oct. 25 and Nov. 4 were largely distributed to employee break rooms, refrigerated vending machines and cafeterias (best-by dates of Nov. 7-19).

 Listeria poisoning , or listerosis, is a foodborne bacterial infection most commonly caused by the bacterium Listeria monocytogenes, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. It is considered a serious condition and can be dangerous or life-threatening, especially when contracted by adults over 65, people with weak immune systems and pregnant women.
 Symptoms usually start within two weeks of eating contaminated food, but may begin as early as the same day or as late as 10 weeks after. According to the CDC, symptoms include:
 Fever
 Muscle aches
 Headache
 Stiff neck
 Confusion
 Loss of balance
 Convulsions
 Diarrhea
 Other gastrointestinal symptoms
 Miscarriage, stillbirth, premature delivery and/or life-threatening infection of newborn infants
 Death
 People in higher-risk categories who experience flu-like symptoms within two months of consuming contaminated food should seek medical attention. The CDC estimates about 1,250 people get listeria infections annually in the United States and about 172 people die from the infection.
